note: Hebrew merahefet (piel of rahap) describes hovering or fluttering, as a bird over its young (Deut 32:11); "moved" is too vague.
Hebrew yom ehad uses the cardinal "one," not the ordinal "first" used for later days; the KJV smooths it into a series.
Hebrew raqia means something hammered out or spread out, a solid dome; "firmament" (Latin firmamentum) keeps the solidity but is now opaque to most readers.
Hebrew tanninim are large sea monsters or serpents (elsewhere dragons or serpents), not specifically whales.
Hebrew mil'u means simply "fill"; in 1611 "replenish" meant fill, but today it suggests refilling a previously populated earth.
Hebrew le'oklah "for eating"; "meat" meant food in general in 1611, which matters here because the diet given is plants.
